stem:
Bina compares three plans for counting a large sack of identical buttons: the spoken list one, two, three, \ldots ; a list that stops at forty; and a tick mark for each button with no number words.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The spoken list one, two, three, \ldots keeps going and stays usable for a large sack.
The list that stops at forty is enough for any large sack.
Tick marks with no number words are the most usable plan for a large sack.
Any of the three plans works equally well because each uses marks or words.

teacher.key_rationale: A useful count needs an unending standard sequence that is easy to use. The spoken list continues; a list that stops at forty is finite; tick marks can continue but become cumbersome.
